I’ve been feeling on edge for maybe… eight or nine months now. It got worse after something that happened at the pharmacy last year, but I’m not even sure what’s connected to what anymore.

Sleep has been rough. I keep having these really vivid dreams where I’m back in that moment at work and I wake up with my heart racing, sometimes sweating, and it takes a while to realize I’m actually in my own bed. Sometimes it’s not the exact scene, just the same feeling of dread.

Since then, things I used to enjoy—like going out with my friends, reading fiction, even yoga—just feel flat. I go through the motions, but I don’t really care. I catch myself replaying everything and thinking, “If that doctor had listened,” or “If management had staffed us properly, this wouldn’t have happened.” I know it doesn’t change anything, but I fixate on who dropped the ball.

I still feel this kind of frozen terror when my mind goes back to it; it’s like the shock never really wore off. I’m also weirdly jumpy. If someone taps me on the shoulder at work, I practically jump out of my skin. Even small decisions—what to cook, which brand to order for the store—can paralyze me. I’ll stare at options way longer than makes sense, second-guessing everything, like any choice could be the wrong one.
D018-D011_h001.question_a:
It started after the car accident about eight months ago. Since then, it doesn’t feel like it ever really ended. I still see the truck coming at us when I close my eyes, and at least a few nights a week I jerk awake from these awful dreams where I’m back on that highway. I wake up sweating, heart racing, and it takes me a minute to remember I’m in my own bed.

I used to love reading and doing yoga after my shifts at the pharmacy, but now I just…don’t care. My husband keeps suggesting we go hiking like we used to, and I have zero interest. Mostly I just sit on the couch scrolling, feeling stuck on that moment of impact. The terror of it is still right there, like it just happened yesterday. I keep running through it and blaming the other driver, my husband for insisting we take that route, even myself for not insisting we stop earlier.

Day to day, I’m jumpy and on edge. If someone taps me on the shoulder at work, I practically jump out of my skin. Even simple decisions—what to wear, what to cook—can paralyze me. And the constant anxiety I feel is always tied back to being on the road, crashes, or something bad suddenly happening again.
D018-D011_h001.question_b:
I’ve been on edge for at least the last year, maybe longer. It feels like my mind is constantly scanning for what could go wrong — with my kids, my husband, my parents’ health, money, my job at the pharmacy, even random things like whether I missed an interaction on a prescription. That sense of horror kind of lingers in the background; I still catch myself replaying it and, honestly, blaming the other driver over and over in my head.

I’ve stopped doing things I used to enjoy, like yoga classes or meeting friends after work—partly because I’m so wound up and tired, but not because they remind me of the accident. It all feels like this free‑floating anxiety that’s taken over everything.
